title: Bank of America Stocks Move Lower as Berkshire Cuts Stake Another 5.7%
detail:
Bank of America Stocks Move Lower as Berkshire Cuts Stake Another 5.7%
Khac Phu Nguyen
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:27 PM CST 1 min read
BRK-B
BAC
LEN
BSP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) shares decreased 0.52% to $49.82 at 10:19 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after Berkshire Hathaway's quarterly holdings filing showed another reduction in one of its five largest positions. Berkshire held 455.9 million Bank of America shares at September 30, down 27.5 million, or 5.7%, from June 30.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with BAC.

Is BAC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

BAC GF Value chart

The quarter's sale was worth about $1.5 billion at the September 30 price of $54.43. Berkshire has now sold 57.8 million shares, or 11.2%, since March 31, and the remaining stake equals about 8.2% of its listed equity portfolio. The same filing showed Berkshire nearly doubling its Lennar stake to 26.0 million Class A shares, and it opened a new $689 million position in Bending Spoons.

At today's price the remaining stake is worth about $22.7 billion, roughly $2.1 billion less than at the end of September. A pace of roughly 6% a quarter looks like gradual portfolio management rather than a forced exit, but it removes a steady holder from the shareholder base. GuruFocus gives Bank of America a GF Score of 85/100, driven by strong profitability, while its balance sheet ranking is weak, as is common for leveraged lenders. Its GF Value of $55.41 implies a 10% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued. The next test is whether Berkshire's February filing shows the selling continuing.

title: 79% Upside for NVIDIA? Bank of America Thinks So, and Here’s How
detail:
79% Upside for NVIDIA? Bank of America Thinks So, and Here’s How
Gian Estrada
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 11:01 AM CST 4 min read
NVDA
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
79% Upside for NVIDIA? Bank of America Thinks So, and Here's How ©@Sergei Starostin from Pexels via Canva, @Nana Dua from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bank of America kept its Buy rating and $280 target on NVIDIA on Nov. 16, 79% above the last close, with shares down 35% from their October high.

At $280, NVIDIA would trade at about 23x forward earnings, below the 30x two-year median Bank of America cites.

Price targets have fallen since late October, but fiscal 2028 earnings estimates are still 23% higher than three months ago.

Tuesday's third-quarter report, the first under interim CEO Colette Kress, is the first test of those estimates.

NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) shares are down 35% from their Oct. 6 high, and Bank of America still sees them reaching $280 within a year, 79% above Monday's close of $156.14. Analyst Vivek Arya reiterated his Buy rating and target on Nov. 16, a day before NVIDIA reports its third quarter.

His case doesn't need NVIDIA to beat anyone's numbers. It needs the market to stop pricing the stock like a company in crisis.

A CEO Exit, Then Washington

Jensen Huang resigned as CEO effective Nov. 11, a day before NVIDIA announced it, after admitting an affair with a former executive at a Singapore cloud company whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement.

Washington piled on. On Nov. 15, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said NVIDIA needs "a dramatic shakeup" and urged the board to hire an outside CEO. The same day, Axios reported that he'd questioned whether NVIDIA's earnings were inflated by sales to China. Then on Nov. 17, CNBC reported, citing sources, that NVIDIA had warned customers a proposed law on remote Chinese access to its chips could expose them and the company to U.S. "legal action."

NVIDIA's last report predates all of this. In the quarter ended July 26, revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion, and management guided to $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, for the third quarter.

Why $280 Isn't a Stretch for NVIDIA

Arya cut his target from $350 to $280 on Nov. 12, and it still sits above the new targets from Morgan Stanley, UBS, Mizuho and TD Cowen, which all cut to between $200 and $267 over the past week.

The math is simple. Analysts expect NVIDIA to earn $12.09 a share over the next 12 months, so $280 is about 23x forward earnings. Bank of America puts the stock's two-year median at 30x. Arya also ran a stress test: if data-center sales went flat in 2028, EPS would still top $15, putting $160 a share at about 10.6x those earnings.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Customers at several major US banks reported problems accessing their accounts and completing transactions on Monday after JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) suffered what it called a software bug in its on-premise hardware systems. The bank said there was no evidence this is cyber-related. JPMorgan shares were down 2.33%, Bank of America Corp. (NYSE:BAC) 1.71% and Capital One Financial Corp. (NYSE:COF) 2.83% as of 12:40 p.m. ET.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with JPM.

Is JPM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

JPM GF Value chart

Users at Wells Fargo & Co. (NYSE:WFC) and U.S. Bancorp (NYSE:USB) also reported problems, ranging from logins and transfers to ATMs and banking apps. JPMorgan said other banks may have been affected as parties to its transactions, but that the issue wasnt systemic and customers kept access to their accounts and funds. US Bank said its own systems werent directly affected but that some Zelle payments to other banks could be delayed. Early Warning Services, which runs Zelle, said the network was fully operational, the Telegraph reported.

The outages followed a run of technology failures. Microsofts (NASDAQ:MSFT) email and collaboration services went down late last week, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights nationwide on November 13, and United Airlines (NASDAQ:UAL) suffered a system outage on Monday. Officials have said none of the incidents were cyberattacks, and the White House blamed the FAA disruption on aging systems.

AI Bubble Panic: Wall Street Makes Its Biggest Tech Cut in 20 Years
Lockridge Okoth

BAC
AMZN
MSFT
GOOGN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Fund managers now rank an AI bubble as the biggest threat to global markets, a Bank of America (BofA) survey shows. In a separate BofA poll, European managers' optimism on their own stocks hit its highest level since February.

Europe may not be the escape it looks like. European managers themselves name a US stock or AI valuation correction as the likeliest trigger for a fall in their own market.

Why are Fund Managers Turning Against AI?

In the global survey of 169 investors, managing $461 billion, 34% named an AI bubble their top "tail risk," a rare but damaging shock.

They cut their net overweight in tech to 12%, from 37%, the sharpest monthly cut since June 2006.

Another 31% fear an AI-linked credit crisis. A record 38% say companies are overinvesting.

52% expect at least one hyperscaler, cloud giants such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet, to cut spending within six months. BofA's analysts called a spending pause the survey's "big message," Reuters reported.

The Nasdaq fell more than 5% in October. Fundstrat's Tom Lee still says the AI trade remains intact.

Nvidia, the chipmaker at the center of the AI boom, reports after Tuesday's US close. The results are its first since Jensen Huang quit Nvidia.

Why are Investors Betting on Europe Instead?

Meanwhile, 36% of global managers expect international stocks to perform best in 2027, against 24% for US stocks.

More than two-thirds of European fund managers expect the region's stocks to rise over the next one to three months.

Switzerland and Germany lead, while France sits at a record low of net minus 60%, according to Investing.com.

Fund managers cut their tech overweight to 12% from 37% as European optimism rose to 67%. Source: Bank of America/BeInCrypto

Yet AI and tech are their most crowded theme, at 33%. Crowded trades top their list of portfolio risks.

BofA's own strategist is not buying the rally. Sebastian Raedler has downgraded European stocks to underweight and sees them trailing global peers by about 10% by the second quarter of 2027, Investing.com reported.

The largest US banks hold close to $1 trillion in exposure to AI firms, the Federal Reserve disclosed this month.

title: Berkshire Sells 27.5M Bank of America Shares: Should Investors Worry?
detail:
Berkshire Sells 27.5M Bank of America Shares: Should Investors Worry?
Nikita Kataruka

BAC
JPM
COF

Trading disclosure

Berkshire Hathaway has further reduced its stake in Bank of America BAC, raising questions about investor confidence in the banking giant. Per its November 16 Form 13F filing, Berkshire sold approximately 27.5 million BAC shares during the third quarter of 2026, reducing its holding by 5.7% to 455.9 million shares. Although the sale was smaller than the earlier speculation of 30-40 million shares, continued reductions could weigh on market sentiment.

The latest transaction marks another quarter of Berkshire trimming its BAC exposure. The conglomerate has reduced its position by approximately 57.8 million shares since March 2026. Such persistent selling by a prominent institutional shareholder could create a sentiment overhang, particularly if investors interpret the move as declining conviction in BAC's near-term upside potential.

However, Berkshire's portfolio adjustments do not necessarily indicate deteriorating fundamentals at Bank of America. The conglomerate continues to hold a substantial stake, valued at approximately $24.8 billion as of September-end. The reductions could reflect portfolio diversification or capital reallocation rather than concerns about the bank's financial health.

Importantly, BAC's underlying earnings prospects remain encouraging. Third-quarter 2026 net interest income increased year over year, supported by asset repricing and lending activity. Management expects approximately 8% net interest income growth in 2026 and at least 8% growth in 2027. Continued deposit stability, loan growth and improving interest income could support profitability despite uncertainty surrounding Berkshire's investment strategy.

Yet, further institutional selling could limit BAC's near-term valuation upside and heighten share-price volatility. Elevated operating expenses, potential credit deterioration and interest-rate uncertainty also warrant attention. While Berkshire's continued stake reductions may unsettle investors, BAC's earnings resilience and favorable net interest income outlook suggest that the selling alone does not undermine its longer-term investment prospects.

How Do BAC's Peers Compare?

The implications of Berkshire's continued stake reductions extend beyond Bank of America, as investors assess the broader outlook for large U.S. banks. JPMorgan Chase JPM, for instance, continues to benefit from its diversified business model, strong deposit franchise and multiple revenue streams. While BAC's net interest income growth prospects remain favorable, JPMorgan's diversified operations provide an additional cushion against interest-rate volatility and potential credit challenges.

Meanwhile, Capital One Financial COF has also witnessed a reduction in Berkshire's ownership. During the third quarter, Berkshire trimmed its Capital One stake by approximately 61.7%, a much sharper percentage decline than the 5.7% reduction in BAC. This suggests that Berkshire's selling activity is not limited to Bank of America and could reflect broader portfolio rebalancing rather than concerns specific to BAC.

Nevertheless, the investment outlook for BAC, JPMorgan and Capital One will largely depend on their respective earnings performance, loan demand, credit quality and interest income trends.
